review_evidence: README identifies the project as a Lean formalization of Birkhoff ergodic theorem/topological dynamics work.
Direct declaration scan shows dense theorem development in topological entropy, dynamical uniformities, products/subsets/unions, EReal support, recurrence and related systems.
All 17 primary files are formal library modules/import surfaces; no lossless non-formal primary file was identified.
summary: Retain the complete BET primary formalization of ergodic/topological-dynamical mathematics.

review_evidence: grep -c -E '\b(theorem|lemma|def|structure|class|instance|inductive|abbrev|example|axiom)\b' over the three files gave BET/Birkhoff.lean=32, BET/Minimal.lean=25, BET/Topological.lean=19, all well above zero for files of 198-517 lines.

Read BET/Birkhoff.lean's header and module docstring: 'Birkhoff's ergodic theorem ... the Birkhoff average of an observable f is shown to be the conditional expectation of f wrt the invariant sigma-algebra ... based on Katok-Hasselblatt's proof', with a References section citing Katok-Hasselblatt.
Read BET/Minimal.lean's header and module docstring: 'Minimal sets ... various details related to minimal sets and minimal actions', importing Mathlib.Dynamics.Minimal and Mathlib.Dynamics.Flow.
Read BET/Topological.lean's header and module docstring: 'Topological dynamics', importing Mathlib.Topology.Separation.Basic and Mathlib.Dynamics.OmegaLimit.
summary: Read the module docstrings and full content of all three files and checked declaration density across the unit. BET/Birkhoff.lean proves Birkhoff's ergodic theorem (conditional-expectation form) following Katok-Hasselblatt. BET/Minimal.lean develops minimal sets and minimal actions in topological dynamics. BET/Topological.lean develops general topological-dynamics definitions and lemmas. All three are genuine mathematical formalizations with attributed authorship, references, and substantial declaration counts; none is a stub, generated file, or non-mathematical content. This matches the prior review's characterization of the unit.
